AssociateGlossaryTerms.name: AssociateGlossaryTerms
AssociateGlossaryTerms.doc: Associates one or more glossary terms with an asset in Glue Data Catalog.

BatchCreatePartition.name: BatchCreatePartition
BatchCreatePartition.doc: Creates one or more partitions in a batch operation.

BatchDeleteConnection.name: BatchDeleteConnection
BatchDeleteConnection.doc: Deletes a list of connection definitions from the Data Catalog.

BatchDeletePartition.name: BatchDeletePartition
BatchDeletePartition.doc: Deletes one or more partitions in a batch operation.

BatchDeleteTable.name: BatchDeleteTable
BatchDeleteTable.doc: Deletes multiple tables at once. After completing this operation, you no longer have access to the table versions and partitions that belong to the deleted table. Glue deletes these "orphaned" resources asynchronously in a timely manner, at the discretion of the service. To ensure the immediate deletion of all related resources, before calling BatchDeleteTable, use DeleteTableVersion or…

BatchDeleteTableVersion.name: BatchDeleteTableVersion
BatchDeleteTableVersion.doc: Deletes a specified batch of versions of a table.

BatchGetBlueprints.name: BatchGetBlueprints
BatchGetBlueprints.doc: Retrieves information about a list of blueprints.

BatchGetCrawlers.name: BatchGetCrawlers
BatchGetCrawlers.doc: Returns a list of resource metadata for a given list of crawler names. After calling the ListCrawlers operation, you can call this operation to access the data to which you have been granted permissions. This operation supports all IAM permissions, including permission conditions that uses tags.

BatchGetCustomEntityTypes.name: BatchGetCustomEntityTypes
BatchGetCustomEntityTypes.doc: Retrieves the details for the custom patterns specified by a list of names.

BatchGetDataQualityResult.name: BatchGetDataQualityResult
BatchGetDataQualityResult.doc: Retrieves a list of data quality results for the specified result IDs.

BatchGetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.name: BatchGetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun
BatchGetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.doc: Retrieves the details of multiple evaluation runs in a single request.

BatchGetDevEndpoints.name: BatchGetDevEndpoints
BatchGetDevEndpoints.doc: Returns a list of resource metadata for a given list of development endpoint names. After calling the ListDevEndpoints operation, you can call this operation to access the data to which you have been granted permissions. This operation supports all IAM permissions, including permission conditions that uses tags.

BatchGetIterableForms.name: BatchGetIterableForms
BatchGetIterableForms.doc: Retrieves multiple items from an iterable form on an asset in Glue Data Catalog in a single request.

BatchGetJobs.name: BatchGetJobs
BatchGetJobs.doc: Returns a list of resource metadata for a given list of job names. After calling the ListJobs operation, you can call this operation to access the data to which you have been granted permissions. This operation supports all IAM permissions, including permission conditions that uses tags.

BatchGetPartition.name: BatchGetPartition
BatchGetPartition.doc: Retrieves partitions in a batch request.

BatchGetTableOptimizer.name: BatchGetTableOptimizer
BatchGetTableOptimizer.doc: Returns the configuration for the specified table optimizers.

BatchGetTriggers.name: BatchGetTriggers
BatchGetTriggers.doc: Returns a list of resource metadata for a given list of trigger names. After calling the ListTriggers operation, you can call this operation to access the data to which you have been granted permissions. This operation supports all IAM permissions, including permission conditions that uses tags.

BatchGetWorkflows.name: BatchGetWorkflows
BatchGetWorkflows.doc: Returns a list of resource metadata for a given list of workflow names. After calling the ListWorkflows operation, you can call this operation to access the data to which you have been granted permissions. This operation supports all IAM permissions, including permission conditions that uses tags.

BatchPutDataQualityStatisticAnnotation.name: BatchPutDataQualityStatisticAnnotation
BatchPutDataQualityStatisticAnnotation.doc: Annotate datapoints over time for a specific data quality statistic. The API requires both profileID and statisticID as part of the InclusionAnnotation input. The API only works for a single statisticId across multiple profiles.

BatchStopJobRun.name: BatchStopJobRun
BatchStopJobRun.doc: Stops one or more job runs for a specified job definition.

BatchUpdatePartition.name: BatchUpdatePartition
BatchUpdatePartition.doc: Updates one or more partitions in a batch operation.

CancelDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.name: CancelDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun
CancelDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.doc: Cancels the specified recommendation run that was being used to generate rules.

CancelDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.name: CancelDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun
CancelDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.doc: Cancels a run where a ruleset is being evaluated against a data source.

CancelMLTaskRun.name: CancelMLTaskRun
CancelMLTaskRun.doc: Cancels (stops) a task run. Machine learning task runs are asynchronous tasks that Glue runs on your behalf as part of various machine learning workflows. You can cancel a machine learning task run at any time by calling CancelMLTaskRun with a task run's parent transform's TransformID and the task run's TaskRunId.

CheckSchemaVersionValidity.name: CheckSchemaVersionValidity
CheckSchemaVersionValidity.doc: Validates the supplied schema. This call has no side effects, it simply validates using the supplied schema using DataFormat as the format. Since it does not take a schema set name, no compatibility checks are performed.

CreateCatalog.name: CreateCatalog
CreateCatalog.doc: Creates a new catalog in the Glue Data Catalog.

CreateClassifier.name: CreateClassifier
CreateClassifier.doc: Creates a classifier in the user's account. This can be a GrokClassifier, an XMLClassifier, a JsonClassifier, or a CsvClassifier, depending on which field of the request is present.

CreateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.name: CreateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings
CreateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.doc: Creates settings for a column statistics task.

CreateConnection.name: CreateConnection
CreateConnection.doc: Creates a connection definition in the Data Catalog. Connections used for creating federated resources require the IAM glue:PassConnection permission.

CreateCrawler.name: CreateCrawler
CreateCrawler.doc: Creates a new crawler with specified targets, role, configuration, and optional schedule. At least one crawl target must be specified, in the s3Targets field, the jdbcTargets field, or the DynamoDBTargets field.

CreateCustomEntityType.name: CreateCustomEntityType
CreateCustomEntityType.doc: Creates a custom pattern that is used to detect sensitive data across the columns and rows of your structured data. Each custom pattern you create specifies a regular expression and an optional list of context words. If no context words are passed only a regular expression is checked.

CreateDatabase.name: CreateDatabase
CreateDatabase.doc: Creates a new database in a Data Catalog.

CreateDataQualityRuleset.name: CreateDataQualityRuleset
CreateDataQualityRuleset.doc: Creates a data quality ruleset with DQDL rules applied to a specified Glue table. You create the ruleset using the Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL). For more information, see the Glue developer guide.

CreateGlossary.name: CreateGlossary
CreateGlossary.doc: Creates a business glossary in Glue Data Catalog. A glossary is a container for glossary terms that define business concepts.

CreateGlossaryTerm.name: CreateGlossaryTerm
CreateGlossaryTerm.doc: Creates a glossary term within a business glossary in Glue Data Catalog.

CreateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.name: CreateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration
CreateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.doc: Creates a new Glue Identity Center configuration to enable integration between Glue and Amazon Web Services IAM Identity Center for authentication and authorization.

CreateIntegration.name: CreateIntegration
CreateIntegration.doc: Creates a Zero-ETL integration in the caller's account between two resources with Amazon Resource Names (ARNs): the SourceArn and TargetArn.

CreateIntegrationResourceProperty.name: CreateIntegrationResourceProperty
CreateIntegrationResourceProperty.doc: This API can be used for setting up the ResourceProperty of the Glue connection (for the source) or Glue database ARN (for the target). These properties can include the role to access the connection or database. To set both source and target properties the same API needs to be invoked with the Glue connection ARN as ResourceArn with SourceProcessingProperties and the Glue database ARN as…

CreateIntegrationTableProperties.name: CreateIntegrationTableProperties
CreateIntegrationTableProperties.doc: This API is used to provide optional override properties for the the tables that need to be replicated. These properties can include properties for filtering and partitioning for the source and target tables. To set both source and target properties the same API need to be invoked with the Glue connection ARN as ResourceArn with SourceTableConfig, and the Glue database ARN as ResourceArn with…

CreateMLTransform.name: CreateMLTransform
CreateMLTransform.doc: Creates an Glue machine learning transform. This operation creates the transform and all the necessary parameters to train it. Call this operation as the first step in the process of using a machine learning transform (such as the FindMatches transform) for deduplicating data. You can provide an optional Description, in addition to the parameters that you want to use for your algorithm. You must…

CreatePartitionIndex.name: CreatePartitionIndex
CreatePartitionIndex.doc: Creates a specified partition index in an existing table.

CreateRegistry.name: CreateRegistry
CreateRegistry.doc: Creates a new registry which may be used to hold a collection of schemas.

CreateSchema.name: CreateSchema
CreateSchema.doc: Creates a new schema set and registers the schema definition. Returns an error if the schema set already exists without actually registering the version. When the schema set is created, a version checkpoint will be set to the first version. Compatibility mode "DISABLED" restricts any additional schema versions from being added after the first schema version. For all other compatibility modes,…

CreateScript.name: CreateScript
CreateScript.doc: Transforms a directed acyclic graph (DAG) into code.

CreateSecurityConfiguration.name: CreateSecurityConfiguration
CreateSecurityConfiguration.doc: Creates a new security configuration. A security configuration is a set of security properties that can be used by Glue. You can use a security configuration to encrypt data at rest. For information about using security configurations in Glue, see Encrypting Data Written by Crawlers, Jobs, and Development Endpoints.

CreateTable.name: CreateTable
CreateTable.doc: Creates a new table definition in the Data Catalog.

CreateTableOptimizer.name: CreateTableOptimizer
CreateTableOptimizer.doc: Creates a new table optimizer for a specific function.

CreateTrigger.name: CreateTrigger
CreateTrigger.doc: Creates a new trigger. Job arguments may be logged. Do not pass plaintext secrets as arguments. Retrieve secrets from a Glue Connection, Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager or other secret management mechanism if you intend to keep them within the Job.

CreateUserDefinedFunction.name: CreateUserDefinedFunction
CreateUserDefinedFunction.doc: Creates a new function definition in the Data Catalog.

DeleteAsset.name: DeleteAsset
DeleteAsset.doc: Deletes an asset from Glue Data Catalog.

DeleteAssetType.name: DeleteAssetType
DeleteAssetType.doc: Deletes an asset type from Glue Data Catalog.

DeleteAttachment.name: DeleteAttachment
DeleteAttachment.doc: Deletes a form attachment from an asset in Glue Data Catalog.

DeleteCatalog.name: DeleteCatalog
DeleteCatalog.doc: Removes the specified catalog from the Glue Data Catalog. After completing this operation, you no longer have access to the databases, tables (and all table versions and partitions that might belong to the tables) and the user-defined functions in the deleted catalog. Glue deletes these "orphaned" resources asynchronously in a timely manner, at the discretion of the service. To ensure the…

DeleteClassifier.name: DeleteClassifier
DeleteClassifier.doc: Removes a classifier from the Data Catalog.

DeleteColumnStatisticsForPartition.name: DeleteColumnStatisticsForPartition
DeleteColumnStatisticsForPartition.doc: Delete the partition column statistics of a column. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is DeletePartition.

DeleteColumnStatisticsForTable.name: DeleteColumnStatisticsForTable
DeleteColumnStatisticsForTable.doc: Retrieves table statistics of columns. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is DeleteTable.

DeleteColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.name: DeleteColumnStatisticsTaskSettings
DeleteColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.doc: Deletes settings for a column statistics task.

DeleteConnection.name: DeleteConnection
DeleteConnection.doc: Deletes a connection from the Data Catalog.

DeleteConnectionType.name: DeleteConnectionType
DeleteConnectionType.doc: Deletes a custom connection type in Glue. The connection type must exist and be registered before it can be deleted. This operation supports cleanup of connection type resources and helps maintain proper lifecycle management of custom connection types.

DeleteCrawler.name: DeleteCrawler
DeleteCrawler.doc: Removes a specified crawler from the Glue Data Catalog, unless the crawler state is RUNNING.

DeleteCustomEntityType.name: DeleteCustomEntityType
DeleteCustomEntityType.doc: Deletes a custom pattern by specifying its name.

DeleteDatabase.name: DeleteDatabase
DeleteDatabase.doc: Removes a specified database from a Data Catalog. After completing this operation, you no longer have access to the tables (and all table versions and partitions that might belong to the tables) and the user-defined functions in the deleted database. Glue deletes these "orphaned" resources asynchronously in a timely manner, at the discretion of the service. To ensure the immediate deletion of all…

DeleteFormType.name: DeleteFormType
DeleteFormType.doc: Deletes a form type from Glue Data Catalog. A form type cannot be deleted if it is still referenced by an asset type.

DeleteGlossary.name: DeleteGlossary
DeleteGlossary.doc: Deletes a business glossary from Glue Data Catalog. A glossary cannot be deleted if it still contains glossary terms.

DeleteGlossaryTerm.name: DeleteGlossaryTerm
DeleteGlossaryTerm.doc: Deletes a glossary term from Glue Data Catalog.

DeleteGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.name: DeleteGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration
DeleteGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.doc: Deletes the existing Glue Identity Center configuration, removing the integration between Glue and Amazon Web Services IAM Identity Center.

DeleteIntegrationResourceProperty.name: DeleteIntegrationResourceProperty
DeleteIntegrationResourceProperty.doc: This API is used for deleting the ResourceProperty of the Glue connection (for the source) or Glue database ARN (for the target).

DeleteIntegrationTableProperties.name: DeleteIntegrationTableProperties
DeleteIntegrationTableProperties.doc: Deletes the table properties that have been created for the tables that need to be replicated.

DeleteJob.name: DeleteJob
DeleteJob.doc: Deletes a specified job definition. If the job definition is not found, no exception is thrown.

DeleteMLTransform.name: DeleteMLTransform
DeleteMLTransform.doc: Deletes an Glue machine learning transform. Machine learning transforms are a special type of transform that use machine learning to learn the details of the transformation to be performed by learning from examples provided by humans. These transformations are then saved by Glue. If you no longer need a transform, you can delete it by calling DeleteMLTransforms. However, any Glue jobs that still…

DeletePartitionIndex.name: DeletePartitionIndex
DeletePartitionIndex.doc: Deletes a specified partition index from an existing table.

DeleteRegistry.name: DeleteRegistry
DeleteRegistry.doc: Delete the entire registry including schema and all of its versions. To get the status of the delete operation, you can call the GetRegistry API after the asynchronous call. Deleting a registry will deactivate all online operations for the registry such as the UpdateRegistry, CreateSchema, UpdateSchema, and RegisterSchemaVersion APIs.

DeleteSchema.name: DeleteSchema
DeleteSchema.doc: Deletes the entire schema set, including the schema set and all of its versions. To get the status of the delete operation, you can call GetSchema API after the asynchronous call. Deleting a registry will deactivate all online operations for the schema, such as the GetSchemaByDefinition, and RegisterSchemaVersion APIs.

DeleteSchemaVersions.name: DeleteSchemaVersions
DeleteSchemaVersions.doc: Remove versions from the specified schema. A version number or range may be supplied. If the compatibility mode forbids deleting of a version that is necessary, such as BACKWARDS_FULL, an error is returned. Calling the GetSchemaVersions API after this call will list the status of the deleted versions. When the range of version numbers contain check pointed version, the API will return a 409…

DeleteTable.name: DeleteTable
DeleteTable.doc: Removes a table definition from the Data Catalog. After completing this operation, you no longer have access to the table versions and partitions that belong to the deleted table. Glue deletes these "orphaned" resources asynchronously in a timely manner, at the discretion of the service. To ensure the immediate deletion of all related resources, before calling DeleteTable, use DeleteTableVersion…

DeleteTableOptimizer.name: DeleteTableOptimizer
DeleteTableOptimizer.doc: Deletes an optimizer and all associated metadata for a table. The optimization will no longer be performed on the table.

DeleteTableVersion.name: DeleteTableVersion
DeleteTableVersion.doc: Deletes a specified version of a table.

DeleteTrigger.name: DeleteTrigger
DeleteTrigger.doc: Deletes a specified trigger. If the trigger is not found, no exception is thrown.

DeleteUsageProfile.name: DeleteUsageProfile
DeleteUsageProfile.doc: Deletes the Glue specified usage profile.

DeleteUserDefinedFunction.name: DeleteUserDefinedFunction
DeleteUserDefinedFunction.doc: Deletes an existing function definition from the Data Catalog.

DescribeConnectionType.name: DescribeConnectionType
DescribeConnectionType.doc: The DescribeConnectionType API provides full details of the supported options for a given connection type in Glue. The response includes authentication configuration details that show supported authentication types and properties, and RestConfiguration for custom REST-based connection types registered via RegisterConnectionType. See also: ListConnectionTypes, RegisterConnectionType,…

DescribeEntity.name: DescribeEntity
DescribeEntity.doc: Provides details regarding the entity used with the connection type, with a description of the data model for each field in the selected entity. The response includes all the fields which make up the entity.

DescribeInboundIntegrations.name: DescribeInboundIntegrations
DescribeInboundIntegrations.doc: Returns a list of inbound integrations for the specified integration.

DescribeIntegrations.name: DescribeIntegrations
DescribeIntegrations.doc: The API is used to retrieve a list of integrations.

DisassociateGlossaryTerms.name: DisassociateGlossaryTerms
DisassociateGlossaryTerms.doc: Removes the association of one or more glossary terms from an asset in Glue Data Catalog.

GetAsset.name: GetAsset
GetAsset.doc: Retrieves the metadata for an asset in Glue Data Catalog, including its forms, additional attachments, and associated glossary terms.

GetAssetType.name: GetAssetType
GetAssetType.doc: Retrieves an asset type in Glue Data Catalog by its identifier.

GetBlueprint.name: GetBlueprint
GetBlueprint.doc: Retrieves the details of a blueprint.

GetBlueprintRun.name: GetBlueprintRun
GetBlueprintRun.doc: Retrieves the details of a blueprint run.

GetBlueprintRuns.name: GetBlueprintRuns
GetBlueprintRuns.doc: Retrieves the details of blueprint runs for a specified blueprint.

GetCatalog.name: GetCatalog
GetCatalog.doc: The name of the Catalog to retrieve. This should be all lowercase.

GetCatalogImportStatus.name: GetCatalogImportStatus
GetCatalogImportStatus.doc: Retrieves the status of a migration operation.

GetCatalogs.name: GetCatalogs
GetCatalogs.doc: Retrieves all catalogs defined in a catalog in the Glue Data Catalog. For a Redshift-federated catalog use case, this operation returns the list of catalogs mapped to Redshift databases in the Redshift namespace catalog.

GetClassifiers.name: GetClassifiers
GetClassifiers.doc: Lists all classifier objects in the Data Catalog.

GetColumnStatisticsForPartition.name: GetColumnStatisticsForPartition
GetColumnStatisticsForPartition.doc: Retrieves partition statistics of columns. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is GetPartition.

GetColumnStatisticsForTable.name: GetColumnStatisticsForTable
GetColumnStatisticsForTable.doc: Retrieves table statistics of columns. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is GetTable.

GetColumnStatisticsTaskRun.name: GetColumnStatisticsTaskRun
GetColumnStatisticsTaskRun.doc: Get the associated metadata/information for a task run, given a task run ID.

GetColumnStatisticsTaskRuns.name: GetColumnStatisticsTaskRuns
GetColumnStatisticsTaskRuns.doc: Retrieves information about all runs associated with the specified table.

GetColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.name: GetColumnStatisticsTaskSettings
GetColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.doc: Gets settings for a column statistics task.

GetConnection.name: GetConnection
GetConnection.doc: Retrieves a connection definition from the Data Catalog.

GetConnections.name: GetConnections
GetConnections.doc: Retrieves a list of connection definitions from the Data Catalog.

GetCrawler.name: GetCrawler
GetCrawler.doc: Retrieves metadata for a specified crawler.

GetCrawlers.name: GetCrawlers
GetCrawlers.doc: Retrieves metadata for all crawlers defined in the customer account.

GetCustomEntityType.name: GetCustomEntityType
GetCustomEntityType.doc: Retrieves the details of a custom pattern by specifying its name.

GetDashboardUrl.name: GetDashboardUrl
GetDashboardUrl.doc: Retrieves the URL for the Spark monitoring dashboard for a Glue resource.

GetDatabase.name: GetDatabase
GetDatabase.doc: Retrieves the definition of a specified database.

GetDatabases.name: GetDatabases
GetDatabases.doc: Retrieves all databases defined in a given Data Catalog.

GetDataCatalogEncryptionSettings.name: GetDataCatalogEncryptionSettings
GetDataCatalogEncryptionSettings.doc: Retrieves the security configuration for a specified catalog.

GetDataCatalogExportConfiguration.name: GetDataCatalogExportConfiguration
GetDataCatalogExportConfiguration.doc: Retrieves the current export configuration for the Glue Data Catalog. The export configuration controls whether catalog metadata is exported to S3 Tables.

GetDataflowGraph.name: GetDataflowGraph
GetDataflowGraph.doc: Transforms a Python script into a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

GetDataQualityModel.name: GetDataQualityModel
GetDataQualityModel.doc: Retrieve the training status of the model along with more information (CompletedOn, StartedOn, FailureReason).

GetDataQualityModelResult.name: GetDataQualityModelResult
GetDataQualityModelResult.doc: Retrieve a statistic's predictions for a given Profile ID.

GetDataQualityResult.name: GetDataQualityResult
GetDataQualityResult.doc: Retrieves the result of a data quality rule evaluation.

GetDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.name: GetDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun
GetDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.doc: Gets the specified recommendation run that was used to generate rules.

GetDataQualityRuleset.name: GetDataQualityRuleset
GetDataQualityRuleset.doc: Returns an existing ruleset by identifier or name.

GetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.name: GetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun
GetDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.doc: Retrieves a specific run where a ruleset is evaluated against a data source.

GetDevEndpoint.name: GetDevEndpoint
GetDevEndpoint.doc: Retrieves information about a specified development endpoint. When you create a development endpoint in a virtual private cloud (VPC), Glue returns only a private IP address, and the public IP address field is not populated. When you create a non-VPC development endpoint, Glue returns only a public IP address.

GetDevEndpoints.name: GetDevEndpoints
GetDevEndpoints.doc: Retrieves all the development endpoints in this Amazon Web Services account. When you create a development endpoint in a virtual private cloud (VPC), Glue returns only a private IP address and the public IP address field is not populated. When you create a non-VPC development endpoint, Glue returns only a public IP address.

GetEntityRecords.name: GetEntityRecords
GetEntityRecords.doc: This API is used to query preview data from a given connection type or from a native Amazon S3 based Glue Data Catalog. Returns records as an array of JSON blobs. Each record is formatted using Jackson JsonNode based on the field type defined by the DescribeEntity API. Spark connectors generate schemas according to the same data type mapping as in the DescribeEntity API. Spark connectors convert…

GetFormType.name: GetFormType
GetFormType.doc: Retrieves a form type in Glue Data Catalog by its identifier.

GetGlossary.name: GetGlossary
GetGlossary.doc: Retrieves a business glossary in Glue Data Catalog by its identifier.

GetGlossaryTerm.name: GetGlossaryTerm
GetGlossaryTerm.doc: Retrieves a glossary term in Glue Data Catalog by its identifier.

GetGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.name: GetGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration
GetGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.doc: Retrieves the current Glue Identity Center configuration details, including the associated Identity Center instance and application information.

GetIntegrationResourceProperty.name: GetIntegrationResourceProperty
GetIntegrationResourceProperty.doc: This API is used for fetching the ResourceProperty of the Glue connection (for the source) or Glue database ARN (for the target)

GetIntegrationTableProperties.name: GetIntegrationTableProperties
GetIntegrationTableProperties.doc: This API is used to retrieve optional override properties for the tables that need to be replicated. These properties can include properties for filtering and partition for source and target tables.

GetJobBookmark.name: GetJobBookmark
GetJobBookmark.doc: Returns information on a job bookmark entry. For more information about enabling and using job bookmarks, see: Tracking processed data using job bookmarks Job parameters used by Glue Job structure

GetJobRun.name: GetJobRun
GetJobRun.doc: Retrieves the metadata for a given job run. Job run history is accessible for 365 days for your workflow and job run.

GetJobRuns.name: GetJobRuns
GetJobRuns.doc: Retrieves metadata for all runs of a given job definition. GetJobRuns returns the job runs in chronological order, with the newest jobs returned first.

GetMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.name: GetMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun
GetMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.doc: Get the associated metadata/information for a task run, given a task run ID.

GetMLTaskRun.name: GetMLTaskRun
GetMLTaskRun.doc: Gets details for a specific task run on a machine learning transform. Machine learning task runs are asynchronous tasks that Glue runs on your behalf as part of various machine learning workflows. You can check the stats of any task run by calling GetMLTaskRun with the TaskRunID and its parent transform's TransformID.

GetMLTaskRuns.name: GetMLTaskRuns
GetMLTaskRuns.doc: Gets a list of runs for a machine learning transform. Machine learning task runs are asynchronous tasks that Glue runs on your behalf as part of various machine learning workflows. You can get a sortable, filterable list of machine learning task runs by calling GetMLTaskRuns with their parent transform's TransformID and other optional parameters as documented in this section. This operation…

GetMLTransform.name: GetMLTransform
GetMLTransform.doc: Gets an Glue machine learning transform artifact and all its corresponding metadata. Machine learning transforms are a special type of transform that use machine learning to learn the details of the transformation to be performed by learning from examples provided by humans. These transformations are then saved by Glue. You can retrieve their metadata by calling GetMLTransform.

GetMLTransforms.name: GetMLTransforms
GetMLTransforms.doc: Gets a sortable, filterable list of existing Glue machine learning transforms. Machine learning transforms are a special type of transform that use machine learning to learn the details of the transformation to be performed by learning from examples provided by humans. These transformations are then saved by Glue, and you can retrieve their metadata by calling GetMLTransforms.

GetPartition.name: GetPartition
GetPartition.doc: Retrieves information about a specified partition.

GetPartitionIndexes.name: GetPartitionIndexes
GetPartitionIndexes.doc: Retrieves the partition indexes associated with a table.

GetPartitions.name: GetPartitions
GetPartitions.doc: Retrieves information about the partitions in a table.

GetPlan.name: GetPlan
GetPlan.doc: Gets code to perform a specified mapping.

GetRegistry.name: GetRegistry
GetRegistry.doc: Describes the specified registry in detail.

GetResourcePolicies.name: GetResourcePolicies
GetResourcePolicies.doc: Retrieves the resource policies set on individual resources by Resource Access Manager during cross-account permission grants. Also retrieves the Data Catalog resource policy. If you enabled metadata encryption in Data Catalog settings, and you do not have permission on the KMS key, the operation can't return the Data Catalog resource policy.

GetSchema.name: GetSchema
GetSchema.doc: Describes the specified schema in detail.

GetSchemaByDefinition.name: GetSchemaByDefinition
GetSchemaByDefinition.doc: Retrieves a schema by the SchemaDefinition. The schema definition is sent to the Schema Registry, canonicalized, and hashed. If the hash is matched within the scope of the SchemaName or ARN (or the default registry, if none is supplied), that schema’s metadata is returned. Otherwise, a 404 or NotFound error is returned. Schema versions in Deleted statuses will not be included in the results.

GetSchemaVersion.name: GetSchemaVersion
GetSchemaVersion.doc: Get the specified schema by its unique ID assigned when a version of the schema is created or registered. Schema versions in Deleted status will not be included in the results.

GetSchemaVersionsDiff.name: GetSchemaVersionsDiff
GetSchemaVersionsDiff.doc: Fetches the schema version difference in the specified difference type between two stored schema versions in the Schema Registry. This API allows you to compare two schema versions between two schema definitions under the same schema.

GetSecurityConfigurations.name: GetSecurityConfigurations
GetSecurityConfigurations.doc: Retrieves a list of all security configurations.

GetSessionEndpoint.name: GetSessionEndpoint
GetSessionEndpoint.doc: Returns the Spark Connect endpoint URL and authentication token for an interactive session.

GetTable.name: GetTable
GetTable.doc: Retrieves the Table definition in a Data Catalog for a specified table.

GetTableOptimizer.name: GetTableOptimizer
GetTableOptimizer.doc: Returns the configuration of all optimizers associated with a specified table.

GetTables.name: GetTables
GetTables.doc: Retrieves the definitions of some or all of the tables in a given Database.

GetTableVersion.name: GetTableVersion
GetTableVersion.doc: Retrieves a specified version of a table.

GetTableVersions.name: GetTableVersions
GetTableVersions.doc: Retrieves a list of strings that identify available versions of a specified table.

GetTags.name: GetTags
GetTags.doc: Retrieves a list of tags associated with a resource.

GetTrigger.name: GetTrigger
GetTrigger.doc: Retrieves the definition of a trigger.

GetTriggers.name: GetTriggers
GetTriggers.doc: Gets all the triggers associated with a job.

GetUnfilteredPartitionMetadata.name: GetUnfilteredPartitionMetadata
GetUnfilteredPartitionMetadata.doc: Retrieves partition metadata from the Data Catalog that contains unfiltered metadata. For IAM authorization, the public IAM action associated with this API is glue:GetPartition.

GetUnfilteredPartitionsMetadata.name: GetUnfilteredPartitionsMetadata
GetUnfilteredPartitionsMetadata.doc: Retrieves partition metadata from the Data Catalog that contains unfiltered metadata. For IAM authorization, the public IAM action associated with this API is glue:GetPartitions.

GetUnfilteredTableMetadata.name: GetUnfilteredTableMetadata
GetUnfilteredTableMetadata.doc: Allows a third-party analytical engine to retrieve unfiltered table metadata from the Data Catalog. For IAM authorization, the public IAM action associated with this API is glue:GetTable.

GetUsageProfile.name: GetUsageProfile
GetUsageProfile.doc: Retrieves information about the specified Glue usage profile.

GetUserDefinedFunction.name: GetUserDefinedFunction
GetUserDefinedFunction.doc: Retrieves a specified function definition from the Data Catalog.

GetUserDefinedFunctions.name: GetUserDefinedFunctions
GetUserDefinedFunctions.doc: Retrieves multiple function definitions from the Data Catalog.

GetWorkflow.name: GetWorkflow
GetWorkflow.doc: Retrieves resource metadata for a workflow.

GetWorkflowRun.name: GetWorkflowRun
GetWorkflowRun.doc: Retrieves the metadata for a given workflow run. Job run history is accessible for 90 days for your workflow and job run.

GetWorkflowRunProperties.name: GetWorkflowRunProperties
GetWorkflowRunProperties.doc: Retrieves the workflow run properties which were set during the run.

GetWorkflowRuns.name: GetWorkflowRuns
GetWorkflowRuns.doc: Retrieves metadata for all runs of a given workflow.

ImportCatalogToGlue.name: ImportCatalogToGlue
ImportCatalogToGlue.doc: Imports an existing Amazon Athena Data Catalog to Glue.

ListAssetTypes.name: ListAssetTypes
ListAssetTypes.doc: Lists the asset types defined in Glue Data Catalog.

ListBlueprints.name: ListBlueprints
ListBlueprints.doc: Lists all the blueprint names in an account.

ListColumnStatisticsTaskRuns.name: ListColumnStatisticsTaskRuns
ListColumnStatisticsTaskRuns.doc: List all task runs for a particular account.

ListConnectionTypes.name: ListConnectionTypes
ListConnectionTypes.doc: The ListConnectionTypes API provides a discovery mechanism to learn available connection types in Glue. The response contains a list of connection types with high-level details of what is supported for each connection type, including both built-in connection types and custom connection types registered via RegisterConnectionType. The connection types listed are the set of supported options for…

ListCrawlers.name: ListCrawlers
ListCrawlers.doc: Retrieves the names of all crawler resources in this Amazon Web Services account, or the resources with the specified tag. This operation allows you to see which resources are available in your account, and their names. This operation takes the optional Tags field, which you can use as a filter on the response so that tagged resources can be retrieved as a group. If you choose to use tags…

ListCrawls.name: ListCrawls
ListCrawls.doc: Returns all the crawls of a specified crawler. Returns only the crawls that have occurred since the launch date of the crawler history feature, and only retains up to 12 months of crawls. Older crawls will not be returned. You may use this API to: Retrive all the crawls of a specified crawler. Retrieve all the crawls of a specified crawler within a limited count. Retrieve all the crawls of a…

ListCustomEntityTypes.name: ListCustomEntityTypes
ListCustomEntityTypes.doc: Lists all the custom patterns that have been created.

ListDataQualityResults.name: ListDataQualityResults
ListDataQualityResults.doc: Returns all data quality execution results for your account.

ListDataQualityRuleRecommendationRuns.name: ListDataQualityRuleRecommendationRuns
ListDataQualityRuleRecommendationRuns.doc: Lists the recommendation runs meeting the filter criteria.

ListDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRuns.name: ListDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRuns
ListDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRuns.doc: Lists all the runs meeting the filter criteria, where a ruleset is evaluated against a data source.

ListDataQualityRulesets.name: ListDataQualityRulesets
ListDataQualityRulesets.doc: Returns a paginated list of rulesets for the specified list of Glue tables.

ListDataQualityStatisticAnnotations.name: ListDataQualityStatisticAnnotations
ListDataQualityStatisticAnnotations.doc: Retrieve annotations for a data quality statistic.

ListDataQualityStatistics.name: ListDataQualityStatistics
ListDataQualityStatistics.doc: Retrieves a list of data quality statistics.

ListDevEndpoints.name: ListDevEndpoints
ListDevEndpoints.doc: Retrieves the names of all DevEndpoint resources in this Amazon Web Services account, or the resources with the specified tag. This operation allows you to see which resources are available in your account, and their names. This operation takes the optional Tags field, which you can use as a filter on the response so that tagged resources can be retrieved as a group. If you choose to use tags…

ListEntities.name: ListEntities
ListEntities.doc: Returns the available entities supported by the connection type.

ListFormTypes.name: ListFormTypes
ListFormTypes.doc: Lists the form types defined in Glue Data Catalog.

ListGlossaries.name: ListGlossaries
ListGlossaries.doc: Lists business glossaries in Glue Data Catalog.

ListGlossaryTerms.name: ListGlossaryTerms
ListGlossaryTerms.doc: Lists glossary terms within a business glossary in Glue Data Catalog.

ListIntegrationResourceProperties.name: ListIntegrationResourceProperties
ListIntegrationResourceProperties.doc: List integration resource properties for a single customer. It supports the filters, maxRecords and markers.

ListIterableForms.name: ListIterableForms
ListIterableForms.doc: Lists the items in an iterable form on an asset in Glue Data Catalog. For example, lists the columns of a table asset.

ListJobs.name: ListJobs
ListJobs.doc: Retrieves the names of all job resources in this Amazon Web Services account, or the resources with the specified tag. This operation allows you to see which resources are available in your account, and their names. This operation takes the optional Tags field, which you can use as a filter on the response so that tagged resources can be retrieved as a group. If you choose to use tags filtering,…

ListMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRuns.name: ListMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRuns
ListMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRuns.doc: List all task runs for a particular account.

ListMLTransforms.name: ListMLTransforms
ListMLTransforms.doc: Retrieves a sortable, filterable list of existing Glue machine learning transforms in this Amazon Web Services account, or the resources with the specified tag. This operation takes the optional Tags field, which you can use as a filter of the responses so that tagged resources can be retrieved as a group. If you choose to use tag filtering, only resources with the tags are retrieved.

ListRegistries.name: ListRegistries
ListRegistries.doc: Returns a list of registries that you have created, with minimal registry information. Registries in the Deleting status will not be included in the results. Empty results will be returned if there are no registries available.

ListSchemas.name: ListSchemas
ListSchemas.doc: Returns a list of schemas with minimal details. Schemas in Deleting status will not be included in the results. Empty results will be returned if there are no schemas available. When the RegistryId is not provided, all the schemas across registries will be part of the API response.

ListSchemaVersions.name: ListSchemaVersions
ListSchemaVersions.doc: Returns a list of schema versions that you have created, with minimal information. Schema versions in Deleted status will not be included in the results. Empty results will be returned if there are no schema versions available.

ListTableOptimizerRuns.name: ListTableOptimizerRuns
ListTableOptimizerRuns.doc: Lists the history of previous optimizer runs for a specific table.

ListTriggers.name: ListTriggers
ListTriggers.doc: Retrieves the names of all trigger resources in this Amazon Web Services account, or the resources with the specified tag. This operation allows you to see which resources are available in your account, and their names. This operation takes the optional Tags field, which you can use as a filter on the response so that tagged resources can be retrieved as a group. If you choose to use tags…

ListUsageProfiles.name: ListUsageProfiles
ListUsageProfiles.doc: List all the Glue usage profiles.

ListWorkflows.name: ListWorkflows
ListWorkflows.doc: Lists names of workflows created in the account.

ModifyIntegration.name: ModifyIntegration
ModifyIntegration.doc: Modifies a Zero-ETL integration in the caller's account.

PutAsset.name: PutAsset
PutAsset.doc: Creates or updates an asset in Glue Data Catalog. If the asset already exists, this operation updates it; otherwise, a new asset is created.

PutAssetType.name: PutAssetType
PutAssetType.doc: Creates or updates an asset type in Glue Data Catalog. An asset type defines the structure of assets by specifying which forms they include. If an asset type with the given name already exists, it is updated.

PutAttachment.name: PutAttachment
PutAttachment.doc: Attaches a form to an asset or an iterable form item in Glue Data Catalog. If an attachment with the same name already exists, it is overwritten.

PutDataCatalogEncryptionSettings.name: PutDataCatalogEncryptionSettings
PutDataCatalogEncryptionSettings.doc: Sets the security configuration for a specified catalog. After the configuration has been set, the specified encryption is applied to every catalog write thereafter.

PutDataCatalogExportConfiguration.name: PutDataCatalogExportConfiguration
PutDataCatalogExportConfiguration.doc: Creates or updates the export configuration for the Glue Data Catalog. Use this operation to enable or disable the export of catalog metadata to S3 Tables.

PutDataQualityProfileAnnotation.name: PutDataQualityProfileAnnotation
PutDataQualityProfileAnnotation.doc: Annotate all datapoints for a Profile.

PutFormType.name: PutFormType
PutFormType.doc: Creates or updates a form type in Glue Data Catalog. A form type defines the schema for structured metadata that can be attached to assets.

PutResourcePolicy.name: PutResourcePolicy
PutResourcePolicy.doc: Sets the Data Catalog resource policy for access control.

PutSchemaVersionMetadata.name: PutSchemaVersionMetadata
PutSchemaVersionMetadata.doc: Puts the metadata key value pair for a specified schema version ID. A maximum of 10 key value pairs will be allowed per schema version. They can be added over one or more calls.

PutWorkflowRunProperties.name: PutWorkflowRunProperties
PutWorkflowRunProperties.doc: Puts the specified workflow run properties for the given workflow run. If a property already exists for the specified run, then it overrides the value otherwise adds the property to existing properties.

QuerySchemaVersionMetadata.name: QuerySchemaVersionMetadata
QuerySchemaVersionMetadata.doc: Queries for the schema version metadata information.

RegisterConnectionType.name: RegisterConnectionType
RegisterConnectionType.doc: Registers a custom connection type in Glue based on the configuration provided. This operation enables customers to configure custom connectors for any data source with REST-based APIs, eliminating the need for building custom Lambda connectors. The registered connection type stores details about how requests and responses are interpreted by REST sources, including connection properties,…

RegisterSchemaVersion.name: RegisterSchemaVersion
RegisterSchemaVersion.doc: Adds a new version to the existing schema. Returns an error if new version of schema does not meet the compatibility requirements of the schema set. This API will not create a new schema set and will return a 404 error if the schema set is not already present in the Schema Registry. If this is the first schema definition to be registered in the Schema Registry, this API will store the schema…

RemoveSchemaVersionMetadata.name: RemoveSchemaVersionMetadata
RemoveSchemaVersionMetadata.doc: Removes a key value pair from the schema version metadata for the specified schema version ID.

ResetJobBookmark.name: ResetJobBookmark
ResetJobBookmark.doc: Resets a bookmark entry. For more information about enabling and using job bookmarks, see: Tracking processed data using job bookmarks Job parameters used by Glue Job structure

ResumeWorkflowRun.name: ResumeWorkflowRun
ResumeWorkflowRun.doc: Restarts selected nodes of a previous partially completed workflow run and resumes the workflow run. The selected nodes and all nodes that are downstream from the selected nodes are run.

SearchAssets.name: SearchAssets
SearchAssets.doc: Searches for assets in Glue Data Catalog using full-text search, filters, sorting, and aggregations. Returns matching assets with relevance-ranked results.

SearchTables.name: SearchTables
SearchTables.doc: Searches a set of tables based on properties in the table metadata as well as on the parent database. You can search against text or filter conditions. You can only get tables that you have access to based on the security policies defined in Lake Formation. You need at least a read-only access to the table for it to be returned. If you do not have access to all the columns in the table, these…

StartBlueprintRun.name: StartBlueprintRun
StartBlueprintRun.doc: Starts a new run of the specified blueprint.

StartColumnStatisticsTaskRun.name: StartColumnStatisticsTaskRun
StartColumnStatisticsTaskRun.doc: Starts a column statistics task run, for a specified table and columns.

StartColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule.name: StartColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule
StartColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule.doc: Starts a column statistics task run schedule.

StartCrawler.name: StartCrawler
StartCrawler.doc: Starts a crawl using the specified crawler, regardless of what is scheduled. If the crawler is already running, returns a CrawlerRunningException.

StartCrawlerSchedule.name: StartCrawlerSchedule
StartCrawlerSchedule.doc: Changes the schedule state of the specified crawler to SCHEDULED, unless the crawler is already running or the schedule state is already SCHEDULED.

StartDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.name: StartDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun
StartDataQualityRuleRecommendationRun.doc: Starts a recommendation run that is used to generate rules when you don't know what rules to write. Glue Data Quality analyzes the data and comes up with recommendations for a potential ruleset. You can then triage the ruleset and modify the generated ruleset to your liking. Recommendation runs are automatically deleted after 90 days.

StartDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.name: StartDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun
StartDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun.doc: Once you have a ruleset definition (either recommended or your own), you call this operation to evaluate the ruleset against a data source (Glue table). The evaluation computes results which you can retrieve with the GetDataQualityResult API.

StartExportLabelsTaskRun.name: StartExportLabelsTaskRun
StartExportLabelsTaskRun.doc: Begins an asynchronous task to export all labeled data for a particular transform. This task is the only label-related API call that is not part of the typical active learning workflow. You typically use StartExportLabelsTaskRun when you want to work with all of your existing labels at the same time, such as when you want to remove or change labels that were previously submitted as truth. This…

StartImportLabelsTaskRun.name: StartImportLabelsTaskRun
StartImportLabelsTaskRun.doc: Enables you to provide additional labels (examples of truth) to be used to teach the machine learning transform and improve its quality. This API operation is generally used as part of the active learning workflow that starts with the StartMLLabelingSetGenerationTaskRun call and that ultimately results in improving the quality of your machine learning transform. After the…

StartJobRun.name: StartJobRun
StartJobRun.doc: Starts a job run using a job definition.

StartMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.name: StartMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun
StartMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.doc: Starts a materialized view refresh task run for a specified materialized view.

StartMLEvaluationTaskRun.name: StartMLEvaluationTaskRun
StartMLEvaluationTaskRun.doc: Starts a task to estimate the quality of the transform. When you provide label sets as examples of truth, Glue machine learning uses some of those examples to learn from them. The rest of the labels are used as a test to estimate quality. Returns a unique identifier for the run. You can call GetMLTaskRun to get more information about the stats of the EvaluationTaskRun.

StartMLLabelingSetGenerationTaskRun.name: StartMLLabelingSetGenerationTaskRun
StartMLLabelingSetGenerationTaskRun.doc: Starts the active learning workflow for your machine learning transform to improve the transform's quality by generating label sets and adding labels. When the StartMLLabelingSetGenerationTaskRun finishes, Glue will have generated a "labeling set" or a set of questions for humans to answer. In the case of the FindMatches transform, these questions are of the form, “What is the correct way to…

StartTrigger.name: StartTrigger
StartTrigger.doc: Starts an existing trigger. See Triggering Jobs for information about how different types of trigger are started.

StartWorkflowRun.name: StartWorkflowRun
StartWorkflowRun.doc: Starts a new run of the specified workflow.

StopColumnStatisticsTaskRun.name: StopColumnStatisticsTaskRun
StopColumnStatisticsTaskRun.doc: Stops a task run for the specified table.

StopColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule.name: StopColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule
StopColumnStatisticsTaskRunSchedule.doc: Stops a column statistics task run schedule.

StopCrawler.name: StopCrawler
StopCrawler.doc: If the specified crawler is running, stops the crawl.

StopCrawlerSchedule.name: StopCrawlerSchedule
StopCrawlerSchedule.doc: Sets the schedule state of the specified crawler to NOT_SCHEDULED, but does not stop the crawler if it is already running.

StopMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.name: StopMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun
StopMaterializedViewRefreshTaskRun.doc: Stops a materialized view refresh task run for a specified materialized view.

StopWorkflowRun.name: StopWorkflowRun
StopWorkflowRun.doc: Stops the execution of the specified workflow run.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.doc: Adds tags to a resource. A tag is a label you can assign to an Amazon Web Services resource. In Glue, you can tag only certain resources. For information about what resources you can tag, see Amazon Web Services Tags in Glue.

TestConnection.name: TestConnection
TestConnection.doc: Tests a connection to a service to validate the service credentials that you provide. You can either provide an existing connection name or a TestConnectionInput for testing a non-existing connection input. Providing both at the same time will cause an error. If the action is successful, the service sends back an HTTP 200 response.

UpdateAsset.name: UpdateAsset
UpdateAsset.doc: Updates the name and description of an existing asset in Glue Data Catalog. Only the fields that you provide are updated.

UpdateCatalog.name: UpdateCatalog
UpdateCatalog.doc: Updates an existing catalog's properties in the Glue Data Catalog.

UpdateClassifier.name: UpdateClassifier
UpdateClassifier.doc: Modifies an existing classifier (a GrokClassifier, an XMLClassifier, a JsonClassifier, or a CsvClassifier, depending on which field is present).

UpdateColumnStatisticsForPartition.name: UpdateColumnStatisticsForPartition
UpdateColumnStatisticsForPartition.doc: Creates or updates partition statistics of columns. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is UpdatePartition.

UpdateColumnStatisticsForTable.name: UpdateColumnStatisticsForTable
UpdateColumnStatisticsForTable.doc: Creates or updates table statistics of columns. The Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission required for this operation is UpdateTable.

UpdateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.name: UpdateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings
UpdateColumnStatisticsTaskSettings.doc: Updates settings for a column statistics task.

UpdateConnection.name: UpdateConnection
UpdateConnection.doc: Updates a connection definition in the Data Catalog.

UpdateCrawler.name: UpdateCrawler
UpdateCrawler.doc: Updates a crawler. If a crawler is running, you must stop it using StopCrawler before updating it.

UpdateCrawlerSchedule.name: UpdateCrawlerSchedule
UpdateCrawlerSchedule.doc: Updates the schedule of a crawler using a cron expression.

UpdateDatabase.name: UpdateDatabase
UpdateDatabase.doc: Updates an existing database definition in a Data Catalog.

UpdateDataQualityRuleset.name: UpdateDataQualityRuleset
UpdateDataQualityRuleset.doc: Updates the specified data quality ruleset.

UpdateGlossary.name: UpdateGlossary
UpdateGlossary.doc: Updates a business glossary in Glue Data Catalog.

UpdateGlossaryTerm.name: UpdateGlossaryTerm
UpdateGlossaryTerm.doc: Updates a glossary term in Glue Data Catalog.

UpdateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.name: UpdateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration
UpdateGlueIdentityCenterConfiguration.doc: Updates the existing Glue Identity Center configuration, allowing modification of scopes and permissions for the integration.

UpdateIntegrationResourceProperty.name: UpdateIntegrationResourceProperty
UpdateIntegrationResourceProperty.doc: This API can be used for updating the ResourceProperty of the Glue connection (for the source) or Glue database ARN (for the target). These properties can include the role to access the connection or database. Since the same resource can be used across multiple integrations, updating resource properties will impact all the integrations using it.

UpdateIntegrationTableProperties.name: UpdateIntegrationTableProperties
UpdateIntegrationTableProperties.doc: This API is used to provide optional override properties for the tables that need to be replicated. These properties can include properties for filtering and partitioning for the source and target tables. To set both source and target properties the same API need to be invoked with the Glue connection ARN as ResourceArn with SourceTableConfig, and the Glue database ARN as ResourceArn with…

UpdateJob.name: UpdateJob
UpdateJob.doc: Updates an existing job definition. The previous job definition is completely overwritten by this information.

UpdateJobFromSourceControl.name: UpdateJobFromSourceControl
UpdateJobFromSourceControl.doc: Synchronizes a job from the source control repository. This operation takes the job artifacts that are located in the remote repository and updates the Glue internal stores with these artifacts. This API supports optional parameters which take in the repository information.

UpdateMLTransform.name: UpdateMLTransform
UpdateMLTransform.doc: Updates an existing machine learning transform. Call this operation to tune the algorithm parameters to achieve better results. After calling this operation, you can call the StartMLEvaluationTaskRun operation to assess how well your new parameters achieved your goals (such as improving the quality of your machine learning transform, or making it more cost-effective).

UpdateRegistry.name: UpdateRegistry
UpdateRegistry.doc: Updates an existing registry which is used to hold a collection of schemas. The updated properties relate to the registry, and do not modify any of the schemas within the registry.

UpdateSchema.name: UpdateSchema
UpdateSchema.doc: Updates the description, compatibility setting, or version checkpoint for a schema set. For updating the compatibility setting, the call will not validate compatibility for the entire set of schema versions with the new compatibility setting. If the value for Compatibility is provided, the VersionNumber (a checkpoint) is also required. The API will validate the checkpoint version number for…

UpdateSourceControlFromJob.name: UpdateSourceControlFromJob
UpdateSourceControlFromJob.doc: Synchronizes a job to the source control repository. This operation takes the job artifacts from the Glue internal stores and makes a commit to the remote repository that is configured on the job. This API supports optional parameters which take in the repository information.

UpdateTable.name: UpdateTable
UpdateTable.doc: Updates a metadata table in the Data Catalog.

UpdateTableOptimizer.name: UpdateTableOptimizer
UpdateTableOptimizer.doc: Updates the configuration for an existing table optimizer.

UpdateTrigger.name: UpdateTrigger
UpdateTrigger.doc: Updates a trigger definition. Job arguments may be logged. Do not pass plaintext secrets as arguments. Retrieve secrets from a Glue Connection, Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager or other secret management mechanism if you intend to keep them within the Job.

UpdateUserDefinedFunction.name: UpdateUserDefinedFunction
UpdateUserDefinedFunction.doc: Updates an existing function definition in the Data Catalog.

JobName.doc: The name of a job to be run.

Arguments.doc: The job arguments used when this trigger fires. For this job run, they replace the default arguments set in the job definition itself. You can specify arguments here that your own job-execution script consumes, as well as arguments that Glue itself consumes. For information about how to specify and consume your own Job arguments, see the Calling Glue APIs in Python topic in the developer guide.…

Timeout.doc: The JobRun timeout in minutes. This is the maximum time that a job run can consume resources before it is terminated and enters TIMEOUT status. This overrides the timeout value set in the parent job. Jobs must have timeout values less than 7 days or 10080 minutes. Otherwise, the jobs will throw an exception. When the value is left blank, the timeout is defaulted to 2,880 minutes for Glue version…

SecurityConfiguration.doc: The name of the SecurityConfiguration structure to be used with this action.

NotificationProperty.doc: Specifies configuration properties of a job run notification.

CrawlerName.doc: The name of the crawler to be used with this action.

Action.doc: Defines an action to be initiated by a trigger.

Name.doc: The name of the transform node.

Inputs.doc: Specifies the fields and rows to use as inputs for the aggregate transform.

Groups.doc: Specifies the fields to group by.

Aggs.doc: Specifies the aggregate functions to be performed on specified fields.

Aggregate.doc: Specifies a transform that groups rows by chosen fields and computes the aggregated value by specified function.

Column.doc: Specifies the column on the data set on which the aggregation function will be applied.

AggFunc.doc: Specifies the aggregation function to apply. Possible aggregation functions include: avg countDistinct, count, first, last, kurtosis, max, min, skewness, stddev_samp, stddev_pop, sum, sumDistinct, var_samp, var_pop

AggregateOperation.doc: Specifies the set of parameters needed to perform aggregation in the aggregate transform.

Description.doc: A description of the allowed value.

Value.doc: The value allowed for the property.

AllowedValue.doc: An object representing a value allowed for a property.

Key.doc: The key for the additional connection option.

Value.doc: The value for the additional connection option.

AmazonRedshiftAdvancedOption.doc: Specifies an optional value when connecting to the Redshift cluster.

AccessType.doc: The access type for the Redshift connection. Can be a direct connection or catalog connections.

SourceType.doc: The source type to specify whether a specific table is the source or a custom query.

Connection.doc: The Glue connection to the Redshift cluster.

Schema.doc: The Redshift schema name when working with a direct connection.

Table.doc: The Redshift table name when working with a direct connection.

CatalogDatabase.doc: The name of the Glue Data Catalog database when working with a data catalog.

CatalogTable.doc: The Glue Data Catalog table name when working with a data catalog.

CatalogRedshiftSchema.doc: The Redshift schema name when working with a data catalog.

CatalogRedshiftTable.doc: The database table to read from.

TempDir.doc: The Amazon S3 path where temporary data can be staged when copying out of the database.

IamRole.doc: Optional. The role name use when connection to S3. The IAM role ill default to the role on the job when left blank.

AdvancedOptions.doc: Optional values when connecting to the Redshift cluster.

SampleQuery.doc: The SQL used to fetch the data from a Redshift sources when the SourceType is 'query'.

PreAction.doc: The SQL used before a MERGE or APPEND with upsert is run.

PostAction.doc: The SQL used before a MERGE or APPEND with upsert is run.

Action.doc: Specifies how writing to a Redshift cluser will occur.

TablePrefix.doc: Specifies the prefix to a table.

Upsert.doc: The action used on Redshift sinks when doing an APPEND.

MergeAction.doc: The action used when to detemine how a MERGE in a Redshift sink will be handled.

MergeWhenMatched.doc: The action used when to detemine how a MERGE in a Redshift sink will be handled when an existing record matches a new record.

MergeWhenNotMatched.doc: The action used when to detemine how a MERGE in a Redshift sink will be handled when an existing record doesn't match a new record.

MergeClause.doc: The SQL used in a custom merge to deal with matching records.

CrawlerConnection.doc: Specifies the name of the connection that is associated with the catalog table used.

TableSchema.doc: The array of schema output for a given node.

StagingTable.doc: The name of the temporary staging table that is used when doing a MERGE or APPEND with upsert.

SelectedColumns.doc: The list of column names used to determine a matching record when doing a MERGE or APPEND with upsert.

Name.doc: The name of the Amazon Redshift source.

Data.doc: Specifies the data of the Amazon Reshift source node.

Name.doc: The name of the Amazon Redshift target.

Data.doc: Specifies the data of the Amazon Redshift target node.

Inputs.doc: The nodes that are inputs to the data target.

ProfileId.doc: The Profile ID for the failed annotation.

StatisticId.doc: The Statistic ID for the failed annotation.

FailureReason.doc: The reason why the annotation failed.

Name.doc: The name of the transform node.

Inputs.doc: The data inputs identified by their node names.

Mapping.doc: Specifies the mapping of data property keys in the data source to data property keys in the data target.

ApplyMapping.doc: Specifies a transform that maps data property keys in the data source to data property keys in the data target. You can rename keys, modify the data types for keys, and choose which keys to drop from the dataset.

FormTypeId.doc: The identifier of the form type that defines this form's schema.

Content.doc: The JSON content of the form, conforming to the schema of the specified form type.

AssetFormEntry.doc: A form on an asset, consisting of the form type identifier and its JSON content.

FormTypeIdentifier.doc: The identifier of the referenced form type.

AssetTypeFormReference.doc: A reference to a form type that is included in an asset type.

Id.doc: The identifier of the asset type.

Name.doc: The name of the asset type.

AssetTypeItem.doc: A summary of an asset type.

AssetIdentifier.doc: The unique identifier of the asset to associate glossary terms with.

IterableFormName.doc: The name of the iterable form. When specified along with itemIdentifier, the glossary terms are associated with an item within the iterable form rather than the asset itself.

ItemIdentifier.doc: The identifier of the item within the iterable form. Required when iterableFormName is specified.

GlossaryTermIdentifiers.doc: The list of glossary term identifiers to associate with the asset.

ClientToken.doc: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure the idempotency of the request.

AssetIdentifier.doc: The unique identifier of the asset.

IterableFormName.doc: The name of the iterable form, if the association targets an item.

ItemIdentifier.doc: The identifier of the item within the iterable form, if applicable.

GlossaryTerms.doc: The glossary terms now associated with the asset.

Name.doc: The name of the data source.

ConnectionName.doc: The name of the connection that is associated with the connector.

ConnectorName.doc: The name of a connector that assists with accessing the data store in Glue Studio.

ConnectionType.doc: The type of connection, such as marketplace.athena or custom.athena, designating a connection to an Amazon Athena data store.

ConnectionTable.doc: The name of the table in the data source.

SchemaName.doc: The name of the Cloudwatch log group to read from. For example, /aws-glue/jobs/output.

OutputSchemas.doc: Specifies the data schema for the custom Athena source.

AthenaConnectorSource.doc: Specifies a connector to an Amazon Athena data source.

AdditionalAuditContext.doc: A string containing the additional audit context information.

AuditContext.doc: A structure containing the Lake Formation audit context.

AuthenticationType.doc: The type of authentication for a connection.

SecretArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the Secrets Manager.

OAuth2Properties.doc: A map of key-value pairs for the OAuth2 properties. Each value is a a Property object.

BasicAuthenticationProperties.doc: A map of key-value pairs for the OAuth2 properties. Each value is a a Property object.

CustomAuthenticationProperties.doc: A map of key-value pairs for the custom authentication properties. Each value is a a Property object.

AuthConfiguration.doc: The authentication configuration for a connection returned by the DescribeConnectionType API.

AuthenticationType.doc: A structure containing the authentication configuration.

SecretArn.doc: The secret manager ARN to store credentials.

KmsKeyArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the KMS key used to encrypt sensitive authentication information. This key is used to protect credentials and other sensitive data stored within the authentication configuration.

AuthenticationConfiguration.doc: A structure containing the authentication configuration.

AuthenticationType.doc: A structure containing the authentication configuration in the CreateConnection request.

OAuth2Properties.doc: The properties for OAuth2 authentication in the CreateConnection request.

SecretArn.doc: The secret manager ARN to store credentials in the CreateConnection request.

KmsKeyArn.doc: The ARN of the KMS key used to encrypt the connection. Only taken an as input in the request and stored in the Secret Manager.

BasicAuthenticationCredentials.doc: The credentials used when the authentication type is basic authentication.

CustomAuthenticationCredentials.doc: The credentials used when the authentication type is custom authentication.

AuthenticationConfigurationInput.doc: A structure containing the authentication configuration in the CreateConnection request.

AuthorizationCode.doc: An authorization code to be used in the third leg of the AUTHORIZATION_CODE grant workflow. This is a single-use code which becomes invalid once exchanged for an access token, thus it is acceptable to have this value as a request parameter.

PartitionColumn.doc: The name of an integer column that is used for partitioning. This option works only when it's included with lowerBound, upperBound, and numPartitions. This option works the same way as in the Spark SQL JDBC reader.

LowerBound.doc: The minimum value of partitionColumn that is used to decide partition stride.

UpperBound.doc: The maximum value of partitionColumn that is used to decide partition stride.

NumPartitions.doc: The number of partitions. This value, along with lowerBound (inclusive) and upperBound (exclusive), form partition strides for generated WHERE clause expressions that are used to split the partitionColumn.

JobBookmarkKeys.doc: The name of the job bookmark keys on which to sort.

JobBookmarkKeysSortOrder.doc: Specifies an ascending or descending sort order.

DataTypeMapping.doc: Custom data type mapping that builds a mapping from a JDBC data type to an Glue data type. For example, the option "dataTypeMapping":{"FLOAT":"STRING"} maps data fields of JDBC type FLOAT into the Java String type by calling the ResultSet.getString() method of the driver, and uses it to build the Glue record. JDBCConnectorTarget.doc: Specifies a data target that writes to Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet columnar storage.

Exclusions.doc: A list of glob patterns used to exclude from the crawl. For more information, see Catalog Tables with a Crawler.

EnableAdditionalMetadata.doc: Specify a value of RAWTYPES or COMMENTS to enable additional metadata in table responses. RAWTYPES provides the native-level datatype. JdbcTarget.doc: Specifies a JDBC data store to crawl.

Name.doc: The name you assign to this job definition.

When the JobMode field is missing or null, SCRIPT is assigned as the default value.

Name.doc: The name of the transform node.

Inputs.doc: The data inputs identified by their node names.

JoinType.doc: Specifies the type of join to be performed on the datasets.

Columns.doc: A list of the two columns to be joined.

Join.doc: Specifies a transform that joins two datasets into one dataset using a comparison phrase on the specified data property keys. You can use inner, outer, left, right, left semi, and left anti joins.

Keys.doc: The key of the column to be joined.

JoinColumn.doc: Specifies a column to be joined.

Name.doc: The name of the classifier.

CreationTime.doc: The time that this classifier was registered.

LastUpdated.doc: The time that this classifier was last updated.

JsonPath.doc: A JsonPath string defining the JSON data for the classifier to classify. Glue supports a subset of JsonPath, as described in Writing JsonPath Custom Classifiers.

BootstrapServers.doc: A list of bootstrap server URLs, for example, as b-1.vpc-test-2.o4q88o.c6.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9094. This option must be specified in the API call or defined in the table metadata in the Data Catalog.

SecurityProtocol.doc: The protocol used to communicate with brokers. The possible values are "SSL" or "PLAINTEXT".

ConnectionName.doc: The name of the connection.

TopicName.doc: The topic name as specified in Apache Kafka. You must specify at least one of "topicName", "assign" or "subscribePattern".

Assign.doc: The specific TopicPartitions to consume. You must specify at least one of "topicName", "assign" or "subscribePattern".

SubscribePattern.doc: A Java regex string that identifies the topic list to subscribe to. You must specify at least one of "topicName", "assign" or "subscribePattern".

StartingOffsets.doc: The starting position in the Kafka topic to read data from. The possible values are "earliest" or "latest". The default value is "latest".

EndingOffsets.doc: The end point when a batch query is ended. Possible values are either "latest" or a JSON string that specifies an ending offset for each TopicPartition.

PollTimeoutMs.doc: The timeout in milliseconds to poll data from Kafka in Spark job executors. The default value is 512.

NumRetries.doc: The number of times to retry before failing to fetch Kafka offsets. The default value is 3.

RetryIntervalMs.doc: The time in milliseconds to wait before retrying to fetch Kafka offsets. The default value is 10.

MaxOffsetsPerTrigger.doc: The rate limit on the maximum number of offsets that are processed per trigger interval. The specified total number of offsets is proportionally split across topicPartitions of different volumes. The default value is null, which means that the consumer reads all offsets until the known latest offset.

MinPartitions.doc: The desired minimum number of partitions to read from Kafka. The default value is null, which means that the number of spark partitions is equal to the number of Kafka partitions.

IncludeHeaders.doc: Whether to include the Kafka headers. When the option is set to "true", the data output will contain an additional column named "glue_streaming_kafka_headers" with type Array[Struct(key: String, value: String)]. The default value is "false". This option is available in Glue version 3.0 or later only.

AddRecordTimestamp.doc: When this option is set to 'true', the data output will contain an additional column named "__src_timestamp" that indicates the time when the corresponding record received by the topic. The default value is 'false'. This option is supported in Glue version 4.0 or later.

EmitConsumerLagMetrics.doc: When this option is set to 'true', for each batch, it will emit the metrics for the duration between the oldest record received by the topic and the time it arrives in Glue to CloudWatch. The metric's name is "glue.driver.streaming.maxConsumerLagInMs". The default value is 'false'. This option is supported in Glue version 4.0 or later.

StartingTimestamp.doc: The timestamp of the record in the Kafka topic to start reading data from. The possible values are a timestamp string in UTC format of the pattern yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SSZ (where Z represents a UTC timezone offset with a +/-. For example: "2023-04-04T08:00:00+08:00"). Only one of StartingTimestamp or StartingOffsets must be set.

Name.doc: The name of a partition key.

Type.doc: The type of a partition key.

KeySchemaElement.doc: A partition key pair consisting of a name and a type.

EndpointUrl.doc: The URL of the Kinesis endpoint.

StreamName.doc: The name of the Kinesis data stream.

StartingPosition.doc: The starting position in the Kinesis data stream to read data from. The possible values are "latest", "trim_horizon", "earliest", or a timestamp string in UTC format in the pattern yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SSZ (where Z represents a UTC timezone offset with a +/-. For example: "2023-04-04T08:00:00-04:00"). The default value is "latest". Note: Using a value that is a timestamp string in UTC format for…

MaxFetchTimeInMs.doc: The maximum time spent for the job executor to read records for the current batch from the Kinesis data stream, specified in milliseconds (ms). Multiple GetRecords API calls may be made within this time. The default value is 1000.

MaxFetchRecordsPerShard.doc: The maximum number of records to fetch per shard in the Kinesis data stream per microbatch. Note: The client can exceed this limit if the streaming job has already read extra records from Kinesis (in the same get-records call). If MaxFetchRecordsPerShard needs to be strict then it needs to be a multiple of MaxRecordPerRead. The default value is 100000.

MaxRecordPerRead.doc: The maximum number of records to fetch from the Kinesis data stream in each getRecords operation. The default value is 10000.

AddIdleTimeBetweenReads.doc: Adds a time delay between two consecutive getRecords operations. The default value is "False". This option is only configurable for Glue version 2.0 and above.

IdleTimeBetweenReadsInMs.doc: The minimum time delay between two consecutive getRecords operations, specified in ms. The default value is 1000. This option is only configurable for Glue version 2.0 and above.

DescribeShardInterval.doc: The minimum time interval between two ListShards API calls for your script to consider resharding. The default value is 1s.

NumRetries.doc: The maximum number of retries for Kinesis Data Streams API requests. The default value is 3.

RetryIntervalMs.doc: The cool-off time period (specified in ms) before retrying the Kinesis Data Streams API call. The default value is 1000.

MaxRetryIntervalMs.doc: The maximum cool-off time period (specified in ms) between two retries of a Kinesis Data Streams API call. The default value is 10000.

AvoidEmptyBatches.doc: Avoids creating an empty microbatch job by checking for unread data in the Kinesis data stream before the batch is started. The default value is "False".

StreamArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream.

RoleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role to assume using AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS). This role must have permissions for describe or read record operations for the Kinesis data stream. You must use this parameter when accessing a data stream in a different account. Used in conjunction with "awsSTSSessionName".

RoleSessionName.doc: An identifier for the session assuming the role using AWS STS. You must use this parameter when accessing a data stream in a different account. Used in conjunction with "awsSTSRoleARN".

AddRecordTimestamp.doc: When this option is set to 'true', the data output will contain an additional column named "__src_timestamp" that indicates the time when the corresponding record received by the stream. The default value is 'false'. This option is supported in Glue version 4.0 or later.

EmitConsumerLagMetrics.doc: When this option is set to 'true', for each batch, it will emit the metrics for the duration between the oldest record received by the stream and the time it arrives in Glue to CloudWatch. The metric's name is "glue.driver.streaming.maxConsumerLagInMs". The default value is 'false'. This option is supported in Glue version 4.0 or later.

StartingTimestamp.doc: The timestamp of the record in the Kinesis data stream to start reading data from. The possible values are a timestamp string in UTC format of the pattern yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SSZ (where Z represents a UTC timezone offset with a +/-. For example: "2023-04-04T08:00:00+08:00").

FanoutConsumerARN.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis Data Streams enhanced fan-out consumer. When specified, enables enhanced fan-out for dedicated throughput and lower latency data consumption.

KinesisStreamingSourceOptions.doc: Additional options for the Amazon Kinesis streaming data source.

OutputS3Path.doc: The Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) path where you will generate the labeling set.

LabelingSetGenerationTaskRunProperties.doc: Specifies configuration properties for a labeling set generation task run.

UseLakeFormationCredentials.doc: Specifies whether to use Lake Formation credentials for the crawler instead of the IAM role credentials.

AccountId.doc: Required for cross account crawls. For same account crawls as the target data, this can be left as null.

LakeFormationConfiguration.doc: Specifies Lake Formation configuration settings for the crawler.
